newsitem.title: USA: Intel at full production, sees robust sales.
newsitem.headline: Intel at full production, sees robust sales.

text.p: Intel Corp Wednesday said its chipmaking factories are at full production, a sign that sales of the company's popular semiconductors are robust.

"My factories are full. We are running pedal to the metal right now. That presumably means sales are pretty robust," Gerhard Parker, executive vice president and general manager of Intel's technology and manufacturing group, told investors at a Montgomery Securities conference here.
Parker said Intel is currently out of capacity. To meet demand for its chips, he said Intel hopes to squeeze out an additional 10 percent of production from existing fabrication plants in 1997.
Intel, the world's largest semiconductor manufacturer, has grown steadily due to strong demand for its popular microprocessors, which power roughly 90 percent of the world's personal computers.
Parker said PC demand looks healthy and said Intel generally agrees with Dataquest Inc's forecast that the PC market is growing at about 18 percent a year.

Intel's most popular product is the Pentium microprocessor. Several times a year it reduces the price of the Pentium chips to fuel sales. In order to reduce those prices, Intel aims for 30 percent production cost savings yearly for the Pentium.
Parker said Intel is currently ahead of its goal having squeezed more efficiencies and achieved higher yields from production.
He said Intel figures it needs to reduce its Pentium manufacturing costs by about 30 percent a year to keep consumer demand for PC's strong.
